businessModel: Quote-based enterprise licensing; venture-funded ($400M Series F in Sept 2026 at a $6.4B valuation)
paidNote: Sold to organizations via demo and quote; no consumer plan or public pricing found
updateCadence: Not published; delivered to managed fleets by the vendor
summary: Island is a Chromium-based enterprise browser that bakes access control, data-loss prevention and activity logging into the browser. Sold to organizations only, on desktop and mobile, and as an extension for other browsers.
bestFor: IT and security teams replacing VDI or locking down BYOD and contractor access
Organizations that need DLP on copy/paste, printing, downloads and screenshots
Companies that want to govern employee AI tool and agent use
Regulated sectors such as finance and healthcare
notFor: Individuals who want a personal browser (no consumer plan found)
Anyone who objects to employer-visible activity logging
Users who want an open-source or auditable browser
Small teams that cannot buy through a sales process

pros.title: Policy depth
pros.detail: Conditional access by identity, device, network and location with device-posture checks and no-code workflow automation.

pros.title: Last-mile data controls
pros.detail: Context-based DLP covers printing, downloads, screenshots and copy/paste while allowing approved app-to-app sharing.

pros.title: Runs where users are
pros.detail: Full browser on Windows, macOS, Linux, ChromeOS and IGEL OS, mobile on iOS and Android, plus an extension for Chrome, Edge, Safari and Firefox.

pros.title: AI governance
pros.detail: Inventories AI agents, maps the MCP servers and extensions they touch, and can block risky AI tools.

pros.title: Work and personal separation
pros.detail: A privacy indicator keeps personal browsing separate from logged work activity.

cons.title: Not for individuals
cons.detail: No public download or pricing; buyers go through a demo and quote.

cons.title: Monitoring by design
cons.detail: It collects data on application interactions to detect unauthorized activity and can record privileged sessions.

cons.title: Closed source
cons.detail: Proprietary build on Chromium, with trust documents available on request rather than public.

cons.title: Little public technical detail
cons.detail: Version numbers, Chromium base, patch cadence and extension (MV2/MV3) handling are not published in the sources reviewed.

faq.q: Can I download Island for personal use?
faq.a: No consumer plan was found; Island is sold to organizations through demos and quotes.
Yes. SiliconANGLE and Island's own page say it is based on Chromium, and the same features are offered as an extension for other browsers.
Founded in 2020 by Mike Fey (CEO, ex-Symantec) and Dan Amiga (CTO), headquartered in Dallas with R&D in Tel Aviv.
